observation_kind: 62 official source facts cross-validated in four modes plus 10 exact-data blockers; not 258 independent HTTP fetches
m: Official page content was directly read back.
The fact was checked against the publisher's current technical or dataset contract.
The fact was applied as a fail-closed guard to all three preserved candidates.
Publisher role, URL, licence and interpretation limits were retained.
f: Current INSPIRE publication date is 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
London Borough of Haringey is present in the current local-authority index.
Polygons are downloaded by local authority.
A GIS is required to view the downloaded polygons.
Downloading accepts the stated Open Government Licence conditions.
INSPIRE contains a subset of registered freehold land and property.
Polygons show indicative position and extent rather than definitive legal extent.
Every INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID.
The ID relates to a registered title, while the title plan is required for registered extent.
Polygons crossing authority boundaries may appear in both authority files.
INSPIRE local-authority files are published as GML.
Polygon coordinates are captured against the British National Grid.
BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The API exposes over 100 planning and housing datasets through one consistent interface.
Latitude and longitude queries return entities whose geometries cover the supplied point.
A coordinate request may include multiple dataset parameters.
UPRN searches use q and are more precise for registered properties.
Entities can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point.
No results do not prove that no constraints exist because coverage varies.
All 337 local planning authorities can be fetched in one request.
geometry_entity can use an existing entity boundary for spatial filtering.
Custom WKT geometry queries use WGS84 coordinates.
Responses can include next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The screening API has no batch endpoint and uses one request per property.
field, exclude_field and quality parameters can constrain results.
Bulk downloads provide stable snapshots in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON or Parquet where applicable.
Article 4 direction area reports 7,152 records and 112 providers on 31 July 2026.
Article 4 direction reports 3,175 records and 102 providers on 31 July 2026.
Article 4 publishing requires two datasets; area geometry is polygon or multipolygon in WGS84 and can be supplied in open formats.
The composite DTM covers about 99 percent of England at one metre resolution.
The DTM uses the last or only return and removes surface objects to model terrain.
The current composite was produced in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeated coverage uses the newest best-resolution survey.
Composite inputs span 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters organised as 5 km OS National Grid tiles.
Heights are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
LIDAR vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
The composite coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features services are listed.
WCS is an open OGC coverage service supported at version 2.0.1.
The persistent no-year endpoint can return raw elevation pixels.
Published DTM1 stretch statistics are min -409.05, max 978.05, mean 104.63 and standard deviation 107.52.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData is represented by -3.4028235e+38.
The current OS Terrain 50 version date is July 2026.
OS Terrain 50 covers Great Britain and is free OpenData under the OGL.
The product is a bare-earth DTM with regular 50 metre post spacing.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use 10 km squares identified by the south-west National Grid reference.
Grid height data is ASCII, with accompanying GML providing spatial and vertical metadata.
Each 10 km tile contains 200 columns and 200 rows of 50 m cells.
Heights represent pixel centres; rows read west to east and progress south.
Grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
OS Terrain 50 grid height points have been verified at 4 m RMSE.
The product is maintained through an integrated three-to-five-year flying programme.
Grid and contour outputs are interpolated from a source TIN using mass points and breaklines.
XML metadata follows GEMINI and is provided nationally and per tile.
Contours use 10 m intervals and include water boundaries and spot heights.
GML uses unique feature identifiers and EPSG:27700; updates refresh whole tiles rather than change-only features.
